title: Telemetry-driven alert suppressor and automated runbook composer for regional graceful degradation
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem statement: Our on-call team is experiencing high noise from transient degradation signals during cross-region capacity shifts and autoscaling events. These noisy pages increase cognitive load and slow remediation for real user-impacting incidents. We lack a systematic way to derive contextual alert suppression thresholds from observed telemetry and to produce actionable runbooks tailored to the failing region, affected route, and active mitigation knobs (circuit breakers, shedding, routing).

Goal: Implement a telemetry-driven alert suppression component plus an automated runbook composer that: (1) reduces noisy pages by suppressing low-impact transient alerts based on correlating SLO delta, synthetic canary signals, and autoscaler events; (2) auto-generates a concise on-call runbook with prioritized remediation steps, safe rollback commands, and suggested circuit-breaker/load-shedding adjustments; (3) integrates with existing incident automation to execute non-destructive mitigation (traffic weights, temporary shedding) when runbook steps are accepted by on-call; (4) surfaces a post-incident summary and candidate permanent mitigation tasks.

Scope (MVP):
- Telemetry inputs: SRE metrics (p99 latency, error rate), SLO burn rate, region-to-region traffic ratios, autoscaler events, synthetic canary failures, and queue/backlog length.
- Suppression logic: probabilistic hysteresis + impact scoring to suppress pages for events with low user-visible impact and high autocorrelation with autoscaler churn or KV-cache warmups.
- Runbook composer: template-driven generator that fills in cause, hit SLOs, affected routes, quick mitigations (safe toggles), and escalation/rollback steps. Output should be a Markdown snippet that can be posted to Slack/incident tracker.
- Automation hooks: opt-in endpoint for executing pre-approved non-destructive mitigations (reduce batch size, enable rate-limiter, apply temporary routing weights, toggle lightweight shedding).

Non-goals: full ML anomaly detection (we'll reuse existing anomaly signals), long-term capacity planning, or wide-scale re-architecting of routing fabric.

Success metrics:
- Page volume reduction for this alert family by >= 60% for non-SLO-impacting events within 30 days of rollout.
- Median time to acknowledgment for remaining pages reduced by 30%.
- Adoption: >50% of incidents in first 3 weeks using generated runbook steps (opt-in acceptance recorded).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Suppression engine can be toggled per-alert-family and per-region via console; 2) For a simulated autoscaler churn test, suppressed pages are reduced by >=60% while a synthetic SLO regression still pages; 3) Generated runbook contains: one-sentence summary, top 3 cause hypotheses, 3 prioritized mitigation steps with exact CLI/console links, rollback guidance, and escalation contacts; 4) Running an opt-in automated mitigation via the endpoint performs the change and logs audit entry; 5) Post-incident summary artifact is created and linked in incident ticket automatically.
technical_notes:
Design decisions:
- Use a lightweight rules-engine combining (a) short-term rate-of-change of SLO burn, (b) canary-failure correlation window (30s-5m), and (c) autoscaler event correlation to compute a suppression score between 0-1. Apply suppression when score < 0.35 and estimated customer-impact = low.
- Store suppression state in Redis with TTLs keyed by alert-family:region:rolling-window. Persist decisions to Telemetry DB for audit.
- Runbook templates live in repo: infra/sre/runbook-templates/*. Must support variables: {region}, {route}, {p99}, {burn_rate}, {active_mitigations}.
- Expose composer via internal REST API /internal/runbook/generate and Slack slash-command /runbook gen.
- Automation endpoint /internal/mitigate/execute requires OAuth and a two-step ack (on-call click approve then API exec). All actions produce immutable audit events forwarded to CloudTrail/KMS-audited log.
- Circuit-breaker and shedding knobs: expose safe presets (dry-run toggle + live toggle). Core runtime team to provide idempotent CLI commands and RBAC-guarded tokens.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (week 1-2): feature-flagged suppression + composer in staging; runbook Slack integration; manual opt-in workflow only (no direct execution). Run chaos/autoscaler churn tests in staging with synthetic SLOs.
Phase 2 (week 3): small pilot on non-critical customer region (eu-west-2) with real traffic; monitor false-suppression and user-impact metrics; collect on-call feedback.
Phase 3 (week 4-6): enable opt-in automated mitigations for pilot; add console controls and audit stream.
Phase 4 (week 7-8): wider rollout to additional regions and promotion of suppression defaults based on pilot.
Rollback: disable suppression and revert runbook composer to read-only; run quick restore playbooks for affected routes.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for suppression scoring and TTL behavior.
- Integration tests simulating: autoscaler bursts, canary flaps, and KV-cache warmups.
- Load test the composer with 100 concurrent generation requests.
- Staging chaos exercises with canary and SLO fail injection.
- On-call dry run: generate runbooks for past 10 incidents and collect survey feedback from SREs.
runbook_template_example:
# Incident runbook (auto-generated)
Summary: p99 latency spike observed in eu-west-2 affecting /api/generate; SLO burn elevated for 3m (burn_rate=4.8). Hypothesis: regional GPU pool cold start + autoscaler surge.
Top causes: 1) cold model shard loading on scale-up 2) KV cache misses after failover 3) routing storm from client retries
Immediate mitigations (safe -> try first):
1) Toggle 'prefer-warmed' routing for region eu-west-2 (console link: https://console.redwood/route/weights)
   CLI: rwdctl routing set-weight --route /api/generate --region eu-west-2 --weight 0.65
2) Enable temporary shed low-priority embeddings (dry-run then live)
   CLI dry-run: rwdctl shed set --route /api/embeddings --mode dry-run --threshold 0.5
   CLI live: rwdctl shed set --route /api/embeddings --mode live --threshold 0.5
3) If latency persists, apply regional circuit-breaker preset 'gradual-evict-v1'
   CLI: rwdctl cb apply --preset gradual-evict-v1 --region eu-west-2
Escalation: contact SRE on-call (pager) and model-serving team (pager); attach generated telemetry snapshot link.
Rollback: revert routing weight and disable shedding, wait 10m and verify p99 returns below target.
Post-incident tasks: create permanent dashboard, consider prewarming policy for model shard pool.
